messages:
alex: heads-up — while validating AWQ-8bit on the new v2 bring-up I hit repeated tool-args parse failures when we stream responses.

alex: repro is small: prompt asks model to emit a single JSON tool call. on AWQ streaming, chunks break inside strings/brackets and the consumer parser throws. non-streamed output from same model is fine.

alex: example chunk sequence we saw in logs:
```
{"tool": "search", "args": {"q": "find top papers about quantizati
on in llms", "filters": {"year": 2024}}}
```

alex: note the "quantizati
on" split — that split causes JS parser to see an EOF mid-string when we try to assemble incremental tokens.

priya: hmm, streaming should reassemble tokens before handing to parser. are we relying on utf8 chunk boundaries instead of token boundaries? :thinking_face:

miguel: I Instrumented the stream consumer — we're concatenating bytes as they arrive and feeding to JSON.parse once we detect a top-level closing brace. but if a chunk ends with a backslash escape or a multi-byte token, parse fails earlier.

dana: does this reproduce only under AWQ or also GPTQ/FP8?

alex: so far only AWQ-8bit on 4k sequence tests. I ran the exact same prompt against GPTQ and FP8 builds — stream was clean.

miguel: could be tokenizer differences causing tokenization boundaries to include surrogate pairs or broken utf8 sequences. AWQ's decode path returns raw bytes in some configs.

priya: workaround: switch the client to buffer until a full parseable JSON is found (try incremental streaming parser that tolerates partial chunks). but we should fix server side too.

eva: agreed. server should emit well-formed utf8 boundaries or at least emit token boundaries that don't split escapes. maybe set decode_policy: "align_utf8" for AWQ?

alex: quick test plan:
- run AWQ vs GPTQ streaming with identical seeds, temp=0, top_p=1, deterministic sampling
- log chunk boundaries and last byte of each chunk (hex)
- run same with non-stream to confirm final output identical
- run with decode_policy toggles (align_utf8, token_aligned)

miguel: I'll script the collector. thinking: add a small shim that prints chunk index + hex tail and whether chunk ends on a quote/backslash/brace.

dana: also include a test invoking tool call with escaped characters and emojis — those are common breaking points.

infra-bot: deploy: rolling out awq-decoder-fix-test -> staging (job #4421) :rocket:

priya: assigning @miguel to run the AWQ vs GPTQ bakeoff and @alex to validate parser changes in the client. can we get results by EOD?

miguel: ack. starting runs now, will ping with a small table.

alex: patch for client incremental parser is trivial; pushing a draft PR in ~30m.

miguel: preliminary: AWQ chunks often end on multi-byte utf8 continuation bytes for some languages. GPTQ tends to align on token boundaries in this config.

eva: if confirmed, we'll need a short-term mitigation (client buffer + streaming parser) and a long-term fix in runtime's decoder to prefer safe emission boundaries. also add a regression test to our quant bakeoff harness.

priya: thanks. Miguel — please upload raw chunk logs to /evals/quant/streams/1728000000/ once done. Alex — link PR here when up.

miguel: done with first pass, uploading now. I'll include a small script:
```bash
python tools/stream_chunk_inspect.py --model awq-8bit-v2 --prompt tests/funcall/escape.json --out chunks/awq-run1.log
```

alex: PR -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-client/pull/421 (incremental json parser + tests). please review.

priya: good work. after we have log diffs and the staging deploy passes, let's add a note in the onboarding docs about streaming caveats for quant decoders.

miguel: FYI I'm also running AWQ with a config that forces token-aligned emission (decode_policy=token_align). preliminary looks better but perf drops ~3%.

alex: perf hit ok as long as correctness is preserved. we'll gate the policy behind model-profile opt-in for now.

dana: :thumbsup: keep us posted.

infra-bot: job #4421 status -> succeeded (staging).

miguel: upload complete, logs + diff summary at s3://redwood-evals/quant/streams/1728000000/summary.txt

priya: great — closing loop once client PR merges and we cut a staging build with token_align enabled for AWQ.

alex: thanks team.
